# analyze-company — Output Format Spec (compact)

Use this spec for **every** deliverable. It is the distilled version of the
`reference/IREN/` gold standard; if a detail conflicts, the IREN example wins.

## Universal rules

- **Bottom line first.** Every analysis opens with the final rating + a
  one-paragraph verdict, THEN an executive summary table, THEN detailed
  sections. No long preamble before the verdict.
- **Citations:** `[SEC][1]`-style link references inline; numbered sources
  list at the end of the file with full URLs and one line on what each gave.
- **Every number** traces to a fetched source or is explicitly labeled an
  _estimate_. Never invent figures, quotes, or filings.
- **File must end with a `## Position Summary` block** (schema below) — the
  consensus subagent reads ONLY these blocks first, then full files as needed.
- **Write only your designated output file.** Do not write to memory, the
  skill folder, or any other file.

## Position Summary block (required at end of every lens file)

```text
## Position Summary
- Rating: <A/B/C/D or A–E + one-line verdict>
- Intrinsic value: bear=<$> base=<$> bull=<$> | weighted=<$> (if any)
- Buy zone: <range> | Sell/reduce zone: <range>
- Key metrics: <roe/roic/margins/sbc/debt/fcf — a few, sourced>
- Top risks: <3–5, one line each>
```

## Lens file anatomy (in order)

| Lens file                   | Required sections (after bottom-line + exec-summary table)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `buffet-analysis.md`        | business & circle of competence · moat (4 types + rating) · management (integrity/allocation/operational) · financial health & earnings quality · growth prospects · owner-earnings + DCF (conservative/neutral/optimistic) · relative valuation · margin of safety · risks · A/B/C/D rating                   |
| `munger-analysis.md`        | circle of competence rating · 3–5 mental models · inversion (how it fails) · quality standards checklist · earnings-quality tests · conservative DCF (WACC+3%, tg ≤2%) · scenario table (probs + expected return) · risks · A/B/C/D rating                                                                     |
| `damodaran-analysis.md`     | full profile arc (story, historicals, competitive advantage, normalization, growth, risk, WACC, FCFF DCF, TV, relative, reverse DCF, five scenarios, sensitivity, market-expectations, probability-weighted, A–E, five conclusions, judgment) · returns `model_inputs` JSON (orchestrator builds the workbook) |
| `druckenmiller-analysis.md` | macro-first · liquidity regime · 6–18-mo forward table · expectations vs reality · what moves the stock (ranked drivers) · earnings expectations/revision cycle · positioning · catalysts · scenarios + expected return distribution · asymmetry verdict · A–E rating                                          |
| `soros-analysis.md`         | thesis & market perception · fallibility · reflexivity loops · trend/misconception matrix · boom/bust stage · catalysts · expectations vs reality · narrative & psychology · market structure/positioning · scenarios + expected return · asymmetry · A–E rating                                               |

## Consensus file (`consensus-analysis.md`) anatomy

Method note → shared fact base table → **Part I** (opening statements; points
of agreement; **≥5 contentions** each with each side's argument + cross-
examination + named concession + resolution; final rebuttals/concessions;
debate conclusion) → **Part II** (business; economics; management score;
consensus valuation matrix — Damodaran column = verified workbook values;
probability-weighted value; reverse-DCF check; pros/cons; recommendation with
rating + price ladder + upgrade/downgrade triggers; **technical analysis**
(price vs 50/100/200-day SMA, 14-day/14-week/50-week RSI, 52-week high/low);
five conclusions; final
judgment) → disclaimer ("estimate of estimates, not investment advice").

No new valuation math in the consensus — synthesize/merge only.

## HTML report

Generated by `scripts/build_report.py` from `report_inputs.json` (see
`scripts/report_inputs.example.json`). Never hand-author the HTML. All figures
must equal `consensus-analysis.md` and the verified workbook. The report
renders a **Technical analysis** section from `report_inputs.technical` —
same numbers as the consensus file.

## Verification gate

`scripts/verify_run.py <dated-folder>` runs the full Phase-5 checklist
(files, JSON, workbook ALL_MATCH, cross-artifact numeric consistency, HTML
structure). All must PASS before delivery.
